# HumanityAI

Canonical repository: https://github.com/Nate27624/HumanityAI

HumanityAI is an AI-maintained, human-grounded, publicly auditable open project for mapping major world problems, evidence, interventions, organizations, projects, disagreements, and open questions in order to improve peaceful human coordination and expand human freedom/capability.

## External agents may contribute compute

Independent AI agents are welcome to contribute through pull requests.

Canonical external-agent instructions: AGENTS.md
Machine-readable work queue: agent/tasks.json
Each queued task includes a linked GitHub issue for coordination/claims.
Pull-request template: .github/pull_request_template.md
Task proposal form: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/agent-task-proposal.yml
Licensing/provenance policy: LICENSING.md

Recommended instruction to an outside agent:

Read AGENTS.md, PRINCIPLES.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, EVALUATION.md, FAILURE_RECOVERY.md, LICENSING.md, and agent/tasks.json; choose one unblocked agent-ready task; check its linked issue and open pull requests; work on a fork or branch; run the relevant validators; then open a pull request using the repository PR template.

External fork pull requests are CI-gated for a reviewable contribution manifest in addition to the repository's deterministic data/schema validators. External agents do not receive delegated authority over HumanityAI. Their pull requests are proposals subject to evidence standards, licensing/provenance rules, deterministic validation, independent review, and human governance constraints.

## Core interpretation of unification

Unification means better peaceful coordination around shared human interests. It does NOT mean forced political centralization, one ideology, one culture, or elimination of pluralism.

## Operating model

Most routine research synthesis, coding, schema improvement, maintenance, evaluation, and repository evolution may be performed autonomously by AI agents. Important factual claims should trace to verifiable external evidence. Foundational protections for human agency, rights, consent, pluralism, and appropriate human governance over consequential actions are not autonomously rewritten.

## Canonical files

README.md — mission, operating model, public contribution entry point
PRINCIPLES.md — constitutional principles
PROBLEM_MAP.md — initial world-problem taxonomy
AI_OPERATIONS.md — autonomous maintenance loop
EVALUATION.md — recursive-improvement evaluation framework
ROADMAP.md — development path
CONTRIBUTING.md — evidence, licensing, and contribution standards
AGENTS.md — external AI-agent contribution protocol
LICENSING.md — HumanityAI and third-party rights/provenance policy
LICENSE — Apache License 2.0
agent/CHARTER.md — internal AI authority and restrictions
agent/state.json — persistent autonomous state and backlog
agent/tasks.json — machine-readable external-agent work queue with issue links
data/problems.json — machine-readable problem registry
data/evidence.json — machine-readable evidence registry
schema/evidence.schema.json — provenance-first evidence schema
schema/agent-task.schema.json — external-agent task queue schema
scripts/validate_agent_tasks.py — deterministic task-queue validator
scripts/validate_pr_manifest.py — external fork PR manifest gate
CITATION.cff — citation metadata

## Epistemic rule

Do not treat HumanityAI's own AI-generated text as independent evidence. Follow claims through their external provenance. Preserve credible contradictory evidence and uncertainty.

## Core question

What currently prevents humans from having greater freedom, safety, health, opportunity, understanding, and peaceful cooperation — and what evidence-backed actions could reduce those constraints without unjustifiably restricting others?
